prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: receiving to outbound release. Elements/aliases: Inbound Inspection Desk=Cinderbay (checks paperwork, trailer ID/seals, damage; consumes Oversize Load Advisory; records proceed/rework/hold; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note to Yard Gate Controller). Pallet Dimension Scanner=Moonquarry (produces Oversize Load Advisory, not placement authorization). Inbound Pallet Buffer (staging only; unavailable to receipts if path crosses recovery area). North Aisle Stacker Crane=Juniperwake (sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot to WMS; uses Slot Reservation Receipt; stops if destination/path invalid; reports faults). South Aisle Stacker Crane (reduced-speed minimal-travel recovery maneuver). East/West Transfer Conveyors (stopped if they compromise boundary). Conveyor Line Controller=Brasshaven (produces Transfer Induction Ticket; holds uncertain/duplicate transfers and those feeding isolated area). Autonomous Forklift Fleet=Larkspur (produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation; receives hold instruction near recovery area). Yard Gate Controller=Velvetrook (validates arrivals, assigns doors; holds vehicles outside recovery boundary). Outbound Dispatch Sorter (receives Dispatch Wave Amendment). Outbound Checkweigh Scale (Gross Weight Variance Slip if out of tolerance). Shipping Documentation Desk. Safety Zone Controller (sets/maintains controlled boundary, blocks entry), Fire Alarm Panel (Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice); both retain stop/restrict authority. Maintenance Release Terminal=Copperfield (produces Crane Service Release Card; records inspection outcome, repairs, authorizer). Warehouse Management System=Morrowglass (authoritative; releases work, plans waves; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; reconciles locations with sensors before recovery plan: travel envelope, stopping point, stop conditions). Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (verifies personnel clear before recovery; reconciles exceptions/maintenance holds/constraints before releasing normal work); drivers, receiving, yard, maintenance staff, spotter (protected location only). Modes: crane available/fault/inhibited/recovery; pallet held/rework/proceed. Requirements: valid receipt; seals before unloading; damaged segregated; no incompatible allocation under advisory; blocked task records hold reason, last location; failed test keeps inhibited; release needs interlock/limit checks; no work without WMS release; recovery triggered by position discrepancy/obstruction/alarm; personnel outside envelope; unexpected motion/position loss/alarm → immediate stop, reassess; boundary removed only after stop/position test passes and aisle clear

New part:
S195: Normal transfers resume in stages, with the first movements observed for unexpected interference or renewed alarms.
S196: Performance is assessed against transfer throughput, task completion time, equipment availability, and the rate of safely resolved exceptions.
S197: The Warehouse Management System records transaction times and reconciles completed movements against the active shift plan.
S198: At shift start, the Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews open alarms, equipment status, and the previous shift's unresolved work.
S199: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor confirms that operators understand current speed limits, exclusion boundaries, and stop-work criteria.
S200: Autonomous Forklift Fleet receives the Transfer Induction Ticket and validates its destination against the assigned route.
S201: Fleet availability is measured as the proportion of scheduled operating time during which vehicles are ready for service.
S202: Route performance is reviewed using completed tasks, travel time, and the number of blocked or delayed movements.
S203: Safety checks verify that personnel detection, audible warnings, and emergency stops respond before production movement begins.
S204: Safety Zone Controller applies the Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice by maintaining the specified exclusion boundary until release criteria are met.
S205: The shift check confirms that the active boundary is visible to operators and enforced by the applicable control logic.
S206: Juniperwake verifies aisle clearance before resuming a stored-pallet movement and stops if an obstruction is detected.
S207: Moonquarry checks each pallet profile against configured dimensional limits and flags measurements outside tolerance.
S208: Dimensional exceptions are held for review rather than passed forward on an assumed measurement.
S209: The Outbound Checkweigh Scale is checked with a known reference load at the start of the shift and after maintenance.
S210: East Transfer Conveyor demonstrates a controlled restart by running empty at reduced speed for one complete cycle before accepting a pallet.
S211: The restart record includes the initiating authorization, observed speed, cycle result, and any alarm response.
S212: The Conveyor Line Controller inhibits feed if the restart cycle is incomplete or a protective device changes state.
S213: Maintenance Release Terminal status is checked before equipment is returned to automatic service.
S214: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor compares reported downtime with control-system event records at each shift review.
S215: Any unexplained difference is investigated before the affected performance measure is accepted.
S216: Near misses, protective stops, and repeated process delays are reviewed for corrective action and accountable ownership.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
